overview: Founded in 1912 and headquartered in Tokyo, Ebara Corporation is a diversified Japanese industrial manufacturer of pumps, compressors, turbines, chillers and precision machinery, organized into five segments: Building Service & Industrial, Energy, Infrastructure, Environmental Solutions, and Precision Machinery. The latter supplies CMP (chemical mechanical polishing) systems, dry vacuum pumps and other semiconductor-manufacturing equipment, giving Ebara direct exposure to the global AI-driven chip capex cycle alongside its more stable industrial fluid-machinery businesses. Ebara operates globally, with roughly two-thirds of FY2025 revenue generated overseas across Asia, North America, Europe and the Middle East.

business_model.summary: Ebara earns revenue from manufacturing and selling custom and standard pumps, compressors, turbines, chillers, blowers and semiconductor process equipment, plus a growing, higher-margin Service & Support (S&S)/O&M tail (overhauls, spare parts, remote monitoring, long-term maintenance and operate contracts) attached to its large installed base. Precision Machinery (semiconductor capital equipment) is project/cycle-driven and tied to wafer fab equipment (WFE) capex; Energy (custom pumps, compressors, turbines for oil & gas, LNG, power) is also capex-cycle sensitive; Building Service & Industrial, Infrastructure (public-sector water/flood pumps) and Environmental Solutions (waste-to-energy EPC and O&M) are comparatively steadier, driven by replacement demand, public infrastructure spending and long-duration service/O&M contracts.

revenue_streams.name: Energy (custom pumps, compressors, turbines - oil & gas/LNG/power)
Building Service & Industrial (standard pumps, chillers, blowers)
Infrastructure (water/flood-control pumps, mostly Japan public sector)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - semiconductor manufacturers (foundry/logic/memory), oil & gas/petrochemical/power companies, building owners/contractors, municipal/public-sector water and waste authorities
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2025: Japan ~33%, Overseas ~67% (Asia ex-Japan/Taiwan/Korea/China ~39% combined, North America ~12%, Europe ~6%, Middle East ~4%, Others ~4%)

main_competitors: Hitachi, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (industrial pumps/compressors in Japan)
competitive_position.market_position: A top-tier global supplier of CMP systems and dry vacuum pumps for semiconductor manufacturing (long-standing niche leader alongside Applied Materials in CMP since the 1990s), and one of Japan's largest diversified pump/fluid-machinery and turbomachinery manufacturers (Elliott Company, acquired 2000, anchors the US compressor/turbine business). Precision Machinery OP margin (~17-18%) is well above the group average, reflecting technological differentiation; the other four segments are less differentiated, operating in fragmented, moderately competitive industrial-pump and public-infrastructure markets where Ebara competes on breadth, service network and long Japanese public-sector relationships rather than outright technology leadership.

moat_factors.factor: Installed base / switching costs in semiconductor equipment
moat_factors.description: Long qualification cycles for CMP/vacuum-pump tools at fabs, plus a growing high-margin S&S/overhaul business (S&S ratio ~28-30% of Precision Machinery revenue) tied to the installed base
Decades of CMP and dry-vacuum-pump engineering; new products (LA+ gas abatement, EVIS integrated system, panel-level-packaging CMP) address sub-fab space/power constraints and advanced packaging

moat_factors.factor: Scale and breadth in custom/engineered pumps and turbomachinery
moat_factors.description: Elliott Company and Ebara's custom pump/compressor businesses serve large, technically demanding oil & gas/LNG/power projects where qualification and reliability matter
Long-standing relationships supplying Japan's water infrastructure, flood-control and waste-treatment public works, reinforced by national resiliency spending programs
113-year operating history as a trusted Japanese industrial manufacturer, supporting customer and supplier relationships globally

weaknesses: Standard pumps/blowers/chillers (Building Service & Industrial) and Infrastructure are lower-margin, more commoditized and face intensifying price competition, especially from Chinese and regional suppliers
Smaller scale than pure-play semiconductor equipment leaders (Applied Materials, Lam Research, TEL) in R&D budget and global sales reach

Energy segment OP ratio (~12% and falling in FY26) is exposed to oil & gas capex cycles and, as of H1 FY2026, direct earnings drag from Middle East geopolitical disruption and a US plant (Jeannette) operational loss
Heavily Japan/Asia-centric revenue base still carries China real-estate/building-market softness risk in Building Service & Industrial

growth_drivers: AI-driven semiconductor capex supercycle: FY26 WFE market outlook raised from "more than 10% growth" (Feb 2026) to "more than 18% growth" (Aug 2026); Precision Machinery FY26 revenue plan raised from Y400bn to Y425bn and orders plan raised from Y405bn to Y550bn between the two FY26 guidance updates

Expansion of high-margin Service & Support (S&S)/O&M revenue across all segments, leveraging a growing global installed base (dry vacuum pump overhaul network expansion in Taiwan/South Korea; Houston and Abu Dhabi S&S service-center expansion for Energy)

New product development for advanced packaging and panel-level packaging (PLP) CMP/plating systems (Model EAPI, Model UFP) and sub-fab footprint/power-saving solutions (LA+, EVIS) to capture AI/advanced-node demand

Decarbonization/new-energy opportunities: hydrogen (liquid hydrogen pumps, cargo pump type-approval for liquefied hydrogen carriers), ammonia, CCUS, and LNG-related large electric motor-driven compressors

Capacity expansion investment: capex nearly doubled in FY2025 (Y92.2bn vs. Y48.6bn in FY2024, from the cash flow statement) and investing cash flow rose to Y91.2bn, consistent with management's E-Plan 2028 strategy of prioritizing growth capex (including a chemical-recycling pilot plant) ahead of returning free cash flow to shareholders

Medium-term plan (E-Plan 2028) targets: revenue scale of ~Y1.2 trillion, ROIC of 13.0%+ (vs. 11.9% FY2025), ROE 18.0%+ (vs. 15.6%), operating profit ratio 14.5%+ (vs. 11.9%), with Precision Machinery targeted to grow revenue at a 15%+ CAGR FY2025-2028 and reach a 20%+ operating margin and 25%+ ROIC
Japan public infrastructure spending tailwind ("Five-Year Acceleration of National Land Resilience Measures") supporting the Infrastructure segment's flood-control and aging-facility renewal demand
Water infrastructure demand growth in Asia (population growth) and North America (aging-facility refurbishment) for the Infrastructure segment

business.description: Revenue and orders are highly sensitive to semiconductor customer capex and factory-utilization cycles; a prior-expected 'full-scale resumption of capacity investment' lagged initial expectations through most of FY2025 before recovering late in the year, illustrating the segment's volatility

business.risk: China market softness in Building Service & Industrial
business.description: China's building-equipment and real-estate-linked industrial markets remain sluggish, pressuring that segment's China revenue even as data-center/semiconductor-linked industrial demand in China offsets some of the weakness

H1 FY2026 Energy operating profit swung to a loss (-Y0.7bn vs +Y11.1bn in H1 FY2025) due to Middle East-related shipment/field-service delays, a US Jeannette plant operational loss, and hydrogen-business cost inclusion

Elliott Company (US compressors/turbines, Energy segment) alone generates more than 10% of consolidated revenue; a small number of large CMP/pump customers in the semiconductor and oil & gas industries drive outsized swings in orders
Company-identified top risk: recruiting/retention difficulties and rising manager workload, particularly recruiting semiconductor-industry specialists amid intense competition for talent

financial.risk: Negative free cash flow from capacity investment
financial.description: FY2025 operating cash flow of Y40.8bn (down from Y100.9bn in FY2024) against capex of roughly Y92bn (up from ~Y48.6bn) produced negative free cash flow; management is prioritizing growth capex, but sustained negative FCF would need to reverse within the E-Plan 2028 3-year free-cash-flow-based shareholder-return framework

Two-thirds of revenue is overseas (USD, EUR, CNY and others); FY26 plan assumes JPY145/USD, a meaningful strengthening assumption from the FY25 average of JPY149.6/USD, creating translation risk either direction

Management targets a D/E ratio of 0.4-0.5 (actual 0.44 at FY2025) to preserve an 'A' credit rating; large capex and M&A could pressure this discipline if growth investment outpaces operating cash flow

regulatory.description: Received a recommendation from the Japan Fair Trade Commission (Feb 2025) under the Act against Delay in Payment of Subcontract Proceeds; launched a Groupwide Fair Procurement Promotion Program and new Legal Revision Response Committee in response

Semiconductor equipment (Precision Machinery) and dual-use industrial equipment exposure to US-China export-control tightening and sanctions regimes; company has expanded its trade-management function for economic security

Scope 1/2 emissions-reduction targets (55% cut by 2030 vs 2018) and EU sustainability-reporting requirements (CSRD/CSDDD) create compliance costs, though these also create product opportunities (decarbonization equipment)

macro.description: As of mid-2026, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are delaying component shipments and field-service engineer dispatches, directly reducing Energy and Building Service & Industrial operating profit (~Y1-2bn direct hit per management's own disclosure), with further escalation risk

A July 2026 Kumamoto earthquake (where Ebara's Kyushu semiconductor-equipment plant is located) halted production lines; as of the August 2026 presentation, no major damage was reported but supply-chain impact was still under assessment

US tariff policy and elevated interest rates are cited as dampening US capital-investment sentiment in Building Service & Industrial's data-center-adjacent industrial market, even as data-center demand itself stays robust

The core bull case rests on continued AI-driven WFE growth; a slowdown in logic/foundry/memory capex (e.g., from AI capex digestion, oversupply, or macro slowdown) would disproportionately hit the highest-margin Precision Machinery segment

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending is forecast to grow strongly in 2026 (estimates from ~11% to over 24% depending on source/scope; Ebara's own management raised its internal FY26 WFE outlook from 'more than 10%' to 'more than 18%' growth between February and August 2026), driven by AI-related logic/foundry and memory/HBM investment. Industrial pump, compressor and water-infrastructure markets grow more slowly but steadily, tied to global capex cycles in oil & gas/LNG/power and to public infrastructure spending.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Mixed - Precision Machinery (semiconductor) and Energy (oil & gas/power capex) are cyclical and capex-linked; Building Service & Industrial, Infrastructure and Environmental Solutions are comparatively defensive, underpinned by replacement demand, Japanese public works and long-term O&M contracts
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via customer capital-investment decisions (e.g., US data-center and building investment described as cautious due to interest-rate uncertainty) and via Ebara's own D/E discipline (0.4-0.5x target) for funding growth capex
key_input_costs: Labor (rising base pay in Japan and overseas)

recent_developments.event: H1 FY2026 results: orders +41.0% YoY to Y636.2bn, revenue +9.4% YoY to Y1,020bn pace (Y490.7bn H1), both record highs for a first half; operating profit roughly flat YoY (+1.2%) as Precision Machinery strength was offset by an Energy segment operating loss

FY2026 guidance raised: orders raised from Y1,070.0bn to Y1,245.0bn (+16.4% vs prior plan) and revenue raised from Y1,020.0bn to Y1,053.0bn (+3.2%); operating profit maintained at Y125.0bn and profit attributable to owners of parent raised to Y99.5bn, as the WFE growth outlook was revised up from 'more than 10%' to 'more than 18%'

Kumamoto earthquake prompted a temporary halt of production lines at Ebara's Kumamoto semiconductor-equipment plant; no major damage reported, but supply-chain impact assessment was ongoing as of the August 2026 presentation

Energy segment operating profit swung to a small loss (-Y0.7bn) due to Middle East geopolitical disruption (delayed shipments/field-service dispatches) and an operational loss at the US Jeannette plant; management expects both issues to resolve and profit to be weighted to H2 FY2026

FY2025 full-year results: orders, revenue, operating profit and profit attributable to owners of parent all reached record highs (revenue Y958.2bn +10.6% YoY; operating profit Y113.8bn +16.2% YoY); annual dividend raised from a forecast Y56 to an actual Y59; Y20bn of treasury shares repurchased in FY2025, with ~5 million shares (1.08% of shares outstanding) scheduled for cancellation Feb 27, 2026

FY2026 initial guidance issued: targeting over Y1 trillion in both orders and revenue for the first time, record operating profit and profit attributable to owners of parent for a sixth straight period, and a dividend increase to Y66/share; share repurchase limit set at Y10bn (down from Y20bn executed in FY2025)
Received a Japan Fair Trade Commission recommendation under the Subcontract Payment Delay Act; launched a Groupwide Fair Procurement Promotion Program and new Legal Revision Response Committee

Analyst sentiment largely positive: consensus rating of 'Buy'/'Strong Buy' across multiple trackers in mid-2026, with average price targets generally in the Y5,800-Y6,400 range (post 5-for-1 split basis) and some brokers (UBS, Goldman Sachs, Macquarie) above Y7,000; SMBC Nikko notably at 'Hold'

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Results Presentation, August 14, 2026 (most recent, superseding the Feb 13, 2026 FY2026 initial plan)

items.notes: Raised from the May 15, 2026 prior plan of ¥1,070.0bn (+16.4%); +31.1% YoY vs FY2025's ¥949.6bn; driven by Precision Machinery orders raised from ¥405.0bn to ¥550.0bn
Raised from ¥1,020.0bn prior plan (+3.2%); +9.9% YoY; first time guided to exceed ¥1 trillion; Precision Machinery revenue plan raised from ¥400.0bn to ¥425.0bn

+9.8% YoY vs FY2025's ¥113.8bn; OP ratio guided at 11.9% (down slightly from 12.3% in the Feb plan); Precision Machinery operating profit plan raised from ¥73.5bn to ¥77.0bn, offset by a lowered Energy segment plan (from ¥21.0bn to ¥18.0bn) partly reflecting a projected pension-related settlement loss

items.metric: Profit Attributable to Owners of Parent
items.notes: +29.8% YoY vs FY2025's ¥76.6bn; EPS guidance of ¥217.93, +31.0% YoY (5-for-1 split-adjusted basis)
FY2025 actual was ROIC 11.9%, ROE 15.6%; FY2028 medium-term targets (E-Plan 2028) are ROIC 13.0%+ and ROE 18.0%+
Up from ¥59.0 actual in FY2025; consolidated payout ratio policy of 35% or higher
FY2025 actual repurchase was ¥20bn; shareholder-return policy targets dividends + buybacks equivalent to 100%+ of cumulative 3-year free cash flow (excluding asset-sale proceeds) under E-Plan 2028

items.metric: Precision Machinery WFE market growth outlook
items.notes: Raised from 'more than 10% growth' guided in the February 2026 presentation, reflecting stronger-than-expected AI-related logic/foundry and memory demand and high customer factory utilization

items.target: Revenue ~¥1.2 trillion scale; OP ratio 14.5%+; D/E 0.4-0.5x; cash on hand 1.5-2.0 months of sales
items.vs_prior: n/a (medium-term plan, not a quarter-to-quarter revision)
items.notes: Precision Machinery segment targets for FY2028: OP ratio 20%+, ROIC 25%+, revenue CAGR FY2025-2028 of 15%+

guidance.management_commentary: Management attributes the FY2026 upward revisions in orders and revenue almost entirely to stronger-than-expected AI-related semiconductor capex (Precision Machinery), while flagging that Energy segment profit was hit in H1 by Middle East-related shipment/service delays and a US plant operational loss, both of which they expect to resolve in H2. Management stated the overall earnings impact from the Middle East situation is 'expected to be limited and is already reflected in the forecast,' and that the July 2026 Kumamoto earthquake caused no major damage to Ebara directly but potential supply-chain impacts remain under assessment. The FY2026 capital allocation stance continues to prioritize growth and 'foundational' investment (including a chemical-recycling pilot plant) while maintaining the 0.4-0.5x D/E discipline and a 35%+ dividend payout ratio, with the share-buyback pace reduced from FY2025's elevated level.

bull_case: Direct, levered exposure to the AI-driven semiconductor capex supercycle through Precision Machinery (CMP, dry vacuum pumps), the group's highest-margin segment (~17-18% OP margin), with management twice raising its FY2026 WFE growth outlook within six months (from 10%+ to 18%+)

Record financial results for multiple consecutive periods (orders, revenue, operating profit and net profit all at all-time highs in FY2025 and again in H1 FY2026), with FY2026 guided to be the first year above Y1 trillion in both orders and revenue

Diversified, less-cyclical base businesses (Building Service & Industrial, Infrastructure, Environmental Solutions) providing earnings ballast and a growing high-margin recurring Service & Support/O&M revenue stream across all five segments

Disciplined capital allocation framework (D/E 0.4-0.5x target, 35%+ dividend payout, buybacks, 100%+ of 3-year cumulative FCF returned to shareholders) alongside credible FY2028 medium-term targets for higher ROIC/ROE/margins
Positive sell-side sentiment with a consensus 'Buy'/'Strong Buy' rating and price targets generally well above recent trading levels as of mid-2026
bear_case: Heavy and growing dependence on a single cyclical end market (semiconductor capex) for the bulk of incremental profit growth; a reversal or digestion phase in AI-related chip investment would disproportionately hit Precision Machinery's premium margins and the stock's growth narrative

FY2025 free cash flow turned negative as capex nearly doubled year-over-year (~Y92bn vs ~Y48.6bn in FY2024) against declining operating cash flow (Y40.8bn vs Y100.9bn), raising execution risk around whether the capacity-expansion investment converts into the targeted FY2028 returns

Energy segment profitability has deteriorated sharply in H1 FY2026 (swinging to an operating loss) due to Middle East geopolitical disruption and a US plant operational loss - a reminder that non-semiconductor segments carry their own project and geopolitical risks

Regulatory/compliance overhang from the February 2025 Japan Fair Trade Commission recommendation on subcontractor payment practices, plus rising export-control and economic-sanctions complexity for semiconductor equipment sales

Natural-disaster exposure illustrated by the July 2026 Kumamoto earthquake affecting a key semiconductor-equipment manufacturing site, alongside China building-market softness weighing on the Building Service & Industrial segment
